transcript_body:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-25 16:00 PDT
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Maya, Liam, Priya (Redwood) — Aisha, Tom, Diego, Sana (Cedarline)

Summary note: audio auto-transcribed; some names/terms may be fuzzy (e.g., 'kay-v cache' for KV cache).

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): ok hey everyone thanks for carving out time today, this is our weekly POC sync for the Dedicated pilot. quick roll call?
00:06 Aisha (Cedarline SRE): hey Aisha here, Tom and Diego on, Sana too.
00:10 Liam (Redwood SE): Liam, infra lead from Redwood, I’ll run the sim and go over policy details.
00:15 Tom (Platform Lead): great, we want to focus on burst behavior and the eviction heuristics, last week's spike caused some errors in staging.
00:22 Maya: yep — we're aiming to make the platform behave predictably under the types of bursts you saw. can you remind us what the staging incident looked like, Tom?
00:30 Tom: sure — roughly 3x traffic for 7 minutes after a callback loop in our mobile app. We had token lengths avg 220, 99th around 450. Our staging used a minimal reserved pool and we saw cold starts and a few 524s.
00:45 Diego (Product PM): also want to reiterate SLOs — p95 generation latency under 800ms and cost target in the pilot of no more than 1.8x our baseline.
00:55 Maya: perfect, those constraints help a lot. quick recap of what Redwood recommends: conservative min pool for prewarm, aggressive burst headroom but with hard caps, and eviction policies that avoid evicting warm KV cache aggressively during short bursts.
01:10 Liam: yes — technical detail: our Dedicated runtime supports a reserve buffer and prewarm triggers. For your profile I'd suggest min=4 GPUs reserved, prewarm_threshold=70% of baseline CPU/GPU usage, max_burst=12 GPUs, cooldown_window=300s. We can tune those numbers after we see your traces.
01:28 Aisha: hmm 4 GPUs min is higher than we expected cost-wise — can we start with min=2 and rely on fast scale up? we saw scale up took ~45s in staging which caused the 524s.
01:38 Liam: scale-up latency depends on instance provisioning and model load time; we have two levers: prewarmed idle workers (min pool) and fast load paths using quantized model variant. If you can accept a slightly lower quality quantized model for burst paths, we can cut load time to ~15s.
01:55 Diego: that's interesting — what's the quality delta on quantized variant? our clinicians are sensitive to hallucinations.
02:02 Liam: it varies by model; for most of the open models we onboarded the delta is small for classification/rerank tasks, slightly larger for open-ended generation. We can run a quick eval on your prompt set.
02:15 Sana (Security): quick pause — any changes to model variants or quantization need to be logged and auditable. we need KMS-backed keys and audit trails for model swaps.
02:24 Maya: totally — Redwood's Private & Dedicated flows keep model versioning and change events in the audit log. we'll include a config change audit for any auto-fallback to quantized variant.
02:34 Tom: ok back to autoscale: you mentioned eviction guardrails — last time some warm KV caches were evicted under memory pressure which made the next requests cost more. What's Redwood's approach?
02:45 Liam: two parts: (1) reserve fraction for cache (we tag worker pools as cache-protected) and (2) eviction priority based on recency + usage signals. short bursts shouldn't trigger aggressive eviction if cache hit rates are > threshold. we can set a conservative eviction cutoff for the POC.
03:05 Aisha: how do you measure cache hit threshold? We don't have precise instrumentation for that yet.
03:10 Liam: we use per-route KV hit metrics; if you can send traces with session ids we can approximate hit rates. otherwise we fallback to a proxy metric: avg tokens served from cache vs total tokens.
03:22 Diego: about burst rehearsals — can you outline the sim you plan to run? we want to understand expected latencies and cost delta for 5x and 10x short spikes.
03:30 Liam: plan: run two simulations, each 2 hours. First sim is synthetic spike profile: baseline traffic + synthetic 5x for 7 minutes every 30 minutes. Second sim replays your anonymized traces at scaled multipliers up to 10x. We'll capture latency percentiles, cold-start counts, cost per token, and worker scale events.
03:48 Maya: we'll upload a spreadsheet with example cost model columns so you can see tokens -> cost. Liam will attach a short readme to explain how to interpret.
03:56 Aisha: timeline question — when can you run the replay? we need results before next product review on April 6.
04:02 Liam: we can run the synthetic sim by Friday night, and replay your traces once you send them — so if traces hit us by Monday we should have a result by Wed/Thu.
04:12 Tom: good. about the autoscale config — can you walk through a conservative HPA-like mapping?
04:18 Liam: sure, simple mapping: target_utilization on token throughput per worker, scale_up_step = +50% workers, scale_down_step = -20% but only after cooldown 10m, max_workers cap is 12 for the POC. also we bind a prewarm pool of 2 workers for fast response so typical short spikes hit prewarm instead of cold start.
04:38 Diego: that scale-up step seems big — won't that overshoot?
04:41 Liam: it's intentional to meet latency SLOs — the tradeoff is cost during the scale window. That's why we pair with a max cap and a shorter cooldown for scale-up than scale-down.
04:50 Priya (CSM): can we model the cost impact under three configs? conservative (min2/max8), medium (min4/max10), aggressive (min6/max12). Liam will produce a small matrix in the sim results.
05:03 Maya: yes, we'll include that. also we'll annotate risk: eviction events, fallback to quantized, and cross-region fallback if a zone is congested.
05:13 Sana: on compliance again — in pilot we need SSO/SAML integration and audit logs accessible via your console or pushed to our syslog.
05:21 Maya: agreed, Redwood supports SAML and audit streaming. I'll share the integration checklist and our SOC2 cert link.
05:28 Aisha: any known gotchas with our VPC peering? we use strict egress controls.
05:33 Liam: generally fine, just ensure mTLS for control plane and open egress to Redwood's control ips/ports; we'll give a minimal whitelist. we'll also provide a Terraform snippet for the peering.
05:44 Diego: last question — if the burst exceeds max_burst and we need to fallback, what's the behavior?
05:49 Liam: automated fallback policy: we first try model variant downgrade to quantized, then deny new requests with 429s (optionally queue), and if routing policy allows we failover to hosted tier with rate-limited proxying. We'll include those failure mode toggles in the playbook.
06:05 Tom: ok that's useful, we prefer 429 over silent long tails.
06:09 Maya: recap of owners and due dates: Maya to share autoscale template + SAML/SOC2 links by 3/30; Liam to run synthetic sim Friday and replay pending traces; Aisha to provide traces by 3/29; Sana to confirm compliance items by 3/31. Meeting after sim review tentatively next Tuesday.
06:28 Diego: all good from product. Thanks everyone.
06:32 Maya: thanks all, we'll post the artifacts to the shared folder after the call.

Notes about transcript quality: speaker turns are approximated, auto-transcription mis-heard 'KV cache' as 'kay-v cache' in some places, and some tokens like 'SOC two' instead of 'SOC 2'.
